name: Hunter eyes surgery

lead: Hunter eyes is looksmaxxing shorthand for a deep-set eye with a positive canthal tilt and little lid show. The surgery people mean by it is usually canthopexy or canthoplasty, sometimes combined with fat grafting or blepharoplasty.

Canthal procedures reposition or suspend the outer lower lid; fat grafting adds volume under the eye or brow; blepharoplasty reshapes lid tissue. Together they aim to change tilt and lid exposure. The surgical literature studies these for lid support and rejuvenation, not for creating this look as a package.

paras: There is no single standard operation by that name, so people usually plan a combination with a facial or oculoplastic surgeon and bring reference photos. Swelling and bruising settle over weeks, and the final shape shows after months.

Reviews describe lid malposition, scleral show, ectropion and shape changes as risks, noting that small changes around the canthus can have large effects. Results as a combined cosmetic package are documented mostly in forum posts.

angle.text: Hunter eyes surgery combines procedures such as canthopexy, fat grafting and blepharoplasty to produce a deep-set, positively tilted eye look, visible after healing. The component surgeries are established, and no study tests the combined goal.

lead: 'Hunter eyes' is looksmaxxing slang for an eye appearance usually described as deep-set, with little upper eyelid show, a low brow-to-lid distance and a neutral or positive canthal tilt, meaning the outer corner sits level with or higher than the inner corner. Wikipedia's looksmaxxing article lists a positive canthal tilt, little upper-eyelid exposure and low-set eyebrows as the defining features and records that Vice reported on the term in June 2023. [1][2][3] 'Hunter eyes surgery' is the community term for surgical combinations intended to produce that look, most often canthopexy or canthoplasty at the outer eye corner, sometimes combined with fat grafting, brow or blepharoplasty procedures. [1]

The appeal for looks is direct: members treat the eye area as a major driver of how intense, alert and attractive a face appears, and see surgery as a way to change tilt and lid exposure for people who do not have the look naturally. [1][4] Wikipedia describes surgery as part of 'hardmaxxing', the branch of looksmaxxing that includes cosmetic surgery such as jaw surgery and rhinoplasty. [2]

There is no single standard operation by that name in the surgical literature. The components are established procedures with other indications: canthopexy and canthoplasty for lower-lid support, lower blepharoplasty, and fat transfer to the periorbital region.  Published studies assess these for lid position, rejuvenation and functional outcomes; no study located evaluates them as a package to create a 'hunter' look.

Canthopexy supports the lower eyelid, typically in conjunction with lower blepharoplasty to reduce the risk of lid malposition, and reviews describe it as the most conservative form of canthal suspension. [5] Because small changes around the lateral canthus can change eyelid shape substantially, reviews call for caution in this area.

paras: In forum usage, 'hunter eyes' refers to eyes seen as intense or predatory, typified by a low lid-to-brow distance and a lateral corner that sits at or above the medial corner. The surgery associated with it is a bundle of procedures rather than one operation; a thread about one member's result describes 'various surgeries combined to get eyes that look as hunter as possible' and attributes the apparent brow elevation to fat grafting. [1]

Wikipedia defines the canthus as the corner of the eye where the upper and lower eyelids meet, with the lateral and medial canthi forming the ends of the palpebral fissure. [3] It also notes that in many East Asian people an epicanthal fold veils the inner canthus, while in other eyes the inner corner is fully exposed. [3] Forum members discuss palpebral fissure length (PFL) and interpupillary distance alongside tilt. [4]

Looksmaxxing began, per Wikipedia, in 2010s incel and manosphere forums, where facial features were ranked with scales such as PSL, before spreading to TikTok in the early 2020s. [2] Eye shape is among the most discussed features, and a looksmax.org thread asked 'when will people who study plastic surgery make a hunter-eyes surgery?', imagining a single procedure that would elongate PFL and change interpupillary distance. [4]

By 2020 and 2021 members were posting about canthopexy as a route to tilt, and one thread shared a member's 'hunter eyes' result a month after surgery. [1] Threads in 2022 and 2025 debate whether pulling the lateral corner adds millimetres of PFL and which procedure suits which patient.  Media interest followed: Wikipedia records that Vice covered hunter eyes in June 2023 within a wave of looksmaxxing coverage that included Business Insider, The New York Times and the BBC. [2]

Canthopexy suspends the lower eyelid to the lateral orbital rim with sutures, while canthoplasty involves detaching and reattaching the lateral canthal tendon. Reviews describe canthopexy as the most conservative option and canthoplasty as reserved for more marked laxity.  Wikipedia describes canthoplasty as plastic surgery on the medial and/or lateral canthus, common in cosmetic procedures and in procedures that address eyelid function or position. [6]

A 1993 article argued that canthopexy should be a routine companion or alternative to lower lid blepharoplasty, restoring lid tone and contour. [5] A 1999 paper presented an algorithm for choosing a method of canthal support in lower eyelid and midfacial rejuvenation and described a simplified suture canthopexy. [7] Later surgical papers describe lateral canthal anchoring and a lateral transorbital canthopexy for correcting and preventing ectropion. [8][9] Anatomical work has mapped the ligamentous attachments of the lower lid and lateral canthus. [10]

Contemporary lower eyelid surgery increasingly includes repositioning of orbital fat to correct inferior orbital hollowing, correcting the negative vector and smoothing the lid-cheek junction.  Wikipedia describes transcutaneous and transconjunctival approaches and notes that fat repositioning and midface elevation may be added to smooth the lid-cheek transition. [11] A 10-year series of lower blepharoplasty with routine lateral canthal support is among the larger reports, and an integrated approach to lower blepharoplasty has also been described. [12][13]
The term blepharoplasty goes back to 1818, when Karl Ferdinand von Graefe coined it; Wikipedia notes that double-eyelid surgery is among the most popular procedures in East Asian countries. [11]

Forum posters credit fat grafting with the apparent brow elevation in a combined result, and 'brow work' is listed with the components that members bundle. [1] A review of midfacial rejuvenation covers the wider region around the lower lid.  No study located evaluates fat grafting as a way to create a hunter look.

Believers hold that eye area proportions strongly affect perceived attractiveness, that canthal tilt and lid exposure can be altered surgically and that a combined plan outperforms any single procedure. [1] Some members say canthopexy is preferable to canthoplasty for people under 40.  Others discuss adding millimetres of PFL.

Researchers have not studied these aims. Surgical reviews describe canthal procedures as supporting the lower lid, and Wikipedia's blepharoplasty article says canthopexy and canthoplasty help maintain eyelid position and may reduce postoperative malposition. [11]

Reviews describe lid malposition, scleral show, ectropion and entropion as the main complications of lower eyelid surgery and canthal work.  Reviews note that canthopexy or canthoplasty is used to reduce the risk of malposition after blepharoplasty. [12] Wikipedia describes ectropion as an outward-turned lower lid that can follow any weakening of lower-lid tissue and can be repaired surgically. [14]
A 10-year, single-surgeon review of 892 blepharoplasty cases examined dry-eye symptoms and chemosis after surgery. [15]

Human studies cover the component procedures in other contexts: a randomised trial of subciliary approaches and lower lid position in infraorbital rim fractures,  a randomised trial of lower eyelid blepharoplasty outcomes and patient satisfaction,  and surgeon case series on canthal support. [12][7] No study located assesses a combined 'hunter eyes' procedure or measures canthal tilt change as an aesthetic outcome.

Members debate canthopexy versus canthoplasty for tilt, with some stating canthopexy is preferable for younger patients, and one thread asks whether pulling the lateral corner adds millimetres of positive 'PFL' (palpebral fissure length).  Members also share before-and-after posts of combined surgeries. [1]

Wikipedia lists maxillofacial surgery as frequently discussed among looksmaxxers and quotes surgeons warning about harms from improvised practices such as bonesmashing; the article does not discuss hunter eyes surgery in that context. [2]

lore.intro: Hunter eyes are treated as a desirable aesthetic target in looksmaxxing, and surgery is discussed as a way to attain them for people without them naturally.[1]

Combined surgeries, including fat grafting, produce a more hunter look than any one procedure.
